claim.quote: Our results, the most sensitive to date with the same target material, NaI(Tl), are incompatible with the DAMA/LIBRA modulation signal at a 4$\sigma$ confidence level.

key_value_text.quote: Such a discrepancy strongly challenges the DAMA/LIBRA dark matter interpretation and highlights the need to address systematic uncertainties affecting the comparison, particularly those related to the response of detectors to nuclear recoils
key_value_text.value: Such a discrepancy strongly challenges the DAMA/LIBRA dark matter interpretation and highlights the need to address systematic uncertainties affecting the comparison, particularly those related to the response of detectors to nuclear recoils, which may require further characterization of the DAMA crystals.

name: Towards a Robust Model-Independent Test of the DAMA/LIBRA Dark Matter Signal: ANAIS-112 Results with Six Years of Data
notes: Published in Physical Review Letters 135 (2025) 051001 according to the experiment's own news page.

published.locator: ANAIS site, news item of 2 October 2025

significance.quote: incompatible with the DAMA/LIBRA modulation signal at a 4$\sigma$ confidence level
significance.value: incompatible with the DAMA/LIBRA modulation signal at a 4 sigma confidence level

summary.plain: After six years of data, ANAIS-112 reports a result incompatible with the DAMA/LIBRA yearly signal at 4 standard deviations. The authors say this strongly challenges the dark matter interpretation but that systematic effects in the comparison, mainly how the crystals respond to recoiling nuclei, need further study.
summary.technical: Annual modulation analysis of six years of ANAIS-112 data (625.75 kg yr exposure per the 2026 review), the most sensitive to date with a NaI(Tl) target; the abstract highlights the need to address systematic uncertainties in the comparison, particularly those related to the detector response to nuclear recoils, which may require further characterisation of the DAMA crystals.

title: Towards a Robust Model-Independent Test of the DAMA/LIBRA Dark Matter Signal: ANAIS-112 Results with Six Years of Data
why_it_matters: The strongest published ANAIS-112 statement on the DAMA/LIBRA signal; a later, still preliminary full-exposure analysis (June 2026 conference news on the ANAIS site) reports no hint of modulation and a sensitivity of about 5 sigma.
